title: fix(core): stop asserting an object has no saved views on a read that never happened (objectui#8900)
body:
Fixes #8900

`Clause-②: yes`

**Why `yes`.** No exported symbol is added and no `.d.ts` byte moves, so the published
TYPE face is unchanged — but the published RUNTIME payload does move: this diff changes
the exact bytes `@object-ui/core`'s exported `elementDataSourceViewNotFoundMessage`
returns and that `@object-ui/react` + `@object-ui/plugin-list` render into a config-error
panel. That string is parsed, not merely displayed: two in-repo consumers matched on the
substring `no saved views`, which is precisely why both had to be rewritten here. Under
the mechanical floor (`when unsure, yes`) a moved published payload is a `yes`.
`needs:contract-review` is applied to this PR as the second carrier.

## The defect

`elementDataSourceViewNotFoundMessage`'s empty-`knownViews` branch ended with
**"This object has no saved views."** — a claim about the OBJECT, derived from a count
that is equally zero in two different worlds:

1. the saved views were read and there are none;
2. the read never successfully happened.

World 2 is the shipped contract, not a bug upstream. `ObjectStackAdapter.listViews`
degrades every failure — refused, offline, malformed — to `[]` on the RESOLVED path
(deliberate; objectui#8151 keeps it), while `useElementDataSource`'s own discrimination
maps only a REJECTION to `undefined` — a shape that contract never produces. So a
refused or broken `view` read arrives at the renderer indistinguishable from a genuine
absence, and the product states as fact something nobody established. A host composing
`@object-ui/react` + `@object-ui/plugin-list` without `app-shell`'s `AdapterProvider`
subscribes to no warning channel at all and sees only that sentence.

## The floor, which is what this PR implements

objectstack#13906 decision 1 option A — *a thing that could not be READ is not a thing
that is ABSENT* — binds this branch. The two worlds are **structurally indistinguishable**
at this point in the code, so the sentence may only assert what is true in BOTH:

> No saved views are known for this object. It may have none, or they could not be read.

Unchanged: the non-empty branch (`Known views: …`), the adapter's degrade-to-empty
contract, and the refusal to fall back to an unfiltered query for the object.

## Route above the floor: none, and the measurement that decided it

I took **the bare floor**. Both enhancements the card names need the failure FACT to
arrive at this consumer, and neither can get it today without reaching into
objectui#8151's fenced surface:

- **Teach the hook to consult `onMetadataReadWarning`.** ⚠️ **A correction to the
  dispatch premise, verified on this branch's base `4fa0eb9c4`:** that channel is NOT
  absent from `main`. `ObjectStackAdapter.onMetadataReadWarning`, `MetadataReadWarningEvent`
  and `app-shell`'s toast sink all landed with objectui#7741 (`listImportMappings`). What is
  absent is any EMITTER for this operation: `listViews`'s catch arm on `main` is still
  exactly `console.warn(...)` then `return []`, with no `emitMetadataReadWarning` call —
  that arm is objectui#8151's delivery and it has not landed. So the route is still
  blocked, for a more precise reason than "the channel does not exist": the channel
  exists and is **silent for `listViews`**. Subscribing to it would pin a fact nothing
  ever emits.
- **A third state on the compose step.** Same wall one hop earlier. `composeElementDataSource`
  and `fetchSavedViews` can only carry a distinction that reaches them, and the only
  failure signal `listViews` produces today is an empty array — which is what BOTH worlds
  produce. Adding a third state now means inferring failure from emptiness, which is the
  one inference that can never be right.

⇒ Neither is a cost trade-off I declined; both are blocked on the same missing emitter.
This PR lands the floor, which is not blocked, and leaves objectui#8151 as the card that
makes "more than this" possible. I did not touch the adapter's catch arm or the warning
channel.

## The pins carried the false claim in their NAMES, so the names changed

Both pins encoded the proposition in the `it()` name as well as in the assertion string;
changing only `toContain(...)` would have left the claim on the record as the named
behaviour under test.

| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/core/src/data-scope/__tests__/element-data-source.test.ts` | `says so plainly when the object has no saved views` | `names both worlds for an empty view list, because it cannot tell them apart` |
| `packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.elementDataSource.test.tsx` | `reports it on an object with no saved views at all` | `reports it without claiming the object has none, when no views came back` |

New, in `plugin-list`: a pair rendered through the real hook and the real gate —
`readFoundNone` (every read succeeds, the object has none) and `readFailed` (the
object-def read rejects and the overlay read reproduces the shipped degrade-to-empty) —
asserting the panel is byte-identical in both. That is the measurement the copy change
rests on, and its `expect(failed).toBe(found)` is a deliberate both-worlds-green control:
it guards the wrong fix of GUESSING which world this is by inferring failure from an
empty array.

## Ablation — the new pins RED before, GREEN after

Mutation leg: source file reverted to base `4fa0eb9c4`, the NEW pins kept. Landing on
disk was proved by anchored counts, not by an editor's exit code — pre-fix sentence
occurrences `1`, post-fix sentence occurrences `0`, and `git hash-object` differing from
the `HEAD` blob. Restore leg was `git checkout HEAD -- PATH` and is proved by `git diff HEAD`
being empty, not by an exit code. Vitest resolves `@object-ui/core` through the root
config's `resolve.alias` to `packages/core/src`, so the ablation reads the mutated SOURCE
and no rebuild sits between the mutation and the assertion.

| assertion | role | source at base | source fixed |
|---|---|---|---|
| core: `msg` not containing `has no saved views` | SUBJECT | **RED** | GREEN |
| core: `msg` containing `could not be read` | SUBJECT | **RED** | GREEN |
| core: `msg` containing the view name and the object name | CONTROL | GREEN | GREEN |
| plugin-list: panel not containing `has no saved views` | SUBJECT | **RED** | GREEN |
| plugin-list: panel containing `could not be read` | SUBJECT | **RED** | GREEN |
| plugin-list: `adapter.find` never called | CONTROL | GREEN | GREEN |
| plugin-list: the two worlds render identically | CONTROL | GREEN | GREEN |

Totals across the two files: **3 failed / 26 passed (29)** at base, **29 passed (29)**
fixed. Every control was green in both legs by measurement, not by assumption.

## Verification

Run on final commit `dc1959733`.

| command | verdict |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/core --filter=@object-ui/plugin-list` | **0** — 15/15 tasks (includes the dependency builds; both packages run `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the pins are type-checked) |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core test` | **0** — 136 files, 2911 tests passed |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-list test` | **0** — 73 files, 895 tests passed |
| `pnpm exec eslint --format json packages/core packages/plugin-list` | **0** — 317 files, 0 errors, 1029 warnings; my three files contribute 0 errors and 0 new warnings (the 4 on the plugin-list pin file are pre-existing `no-explicit-any` at the shared `renderPageComponent` helper and the untouched final test) |
| `pnpm check:element-data-source-declaration` | **0** — 13 gate-consuming files checked |
| `pnpm check:spec-symbols` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:self-import` · `pnpm check:phantom-deps` · `pnpm check:control-bytes` | **0** each |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` · `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` · `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | **0** each |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/registry-assertion-ratchet-8316.test.ts` | **0** — 6 passed (upstream watcher: it names `element-data-source.ts` as its scope-fence NEIGHBOUR) |

Two greens are **NOT readings about this diff** and are reported as such rather than
banked: `pnpm check:unreferenced-sources` covers exactly one package (`packages/components`,
per its own `COVERED_PACKAGES`) and cannot see `@object-ui/core` by design; and
`pnpm check:doc-example-readers` judges JSDoc `@example` blocks, and this diff adds none,
so its population excludes the change by construction.

Content axis, both directions, re-derived by symbol on this branch's base rather than
copied from the card:

- **Downstream** (who calls the message): `ViewDataProvider.resolveElementDataSource` and
  `useElementDataSource` — the only two, both handed `Object.keys(views)`. It is exported
  from `@object-ui/core` via the `data-scope` barrel, named in no README and re-exported
  by no other package.
- **Upstream** (who reads this file's text, path or shape): `scripts/__tests__/registry-assertion-ratchet-8316.test.ts`
  (names the path as its ESLint scope-fence neighbour — run, green) and the two pins.
  `apps/console`'s gate-injection probe renders an unresolvable view but keys on the
  panel's `data-testid` only, never on the sentence. No doc, locale pack or e2e spec
  quotes it.

## 验收备注 — measured, deliberately NOT fixed here

`packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` carries the same empty-equals-absent shape
one surface over — it logs `falling back to the default view. Known views: …` and, above
it, a comment reading *"Adapters without it surface no saved views."* Distinct file,
distinct package, distinct behaviour (it FALLS BACK where this one refuses to), so it is
noted rather than absorbed. Not filed: it is a live observation, not a reproduced defect,
and the successor that would carry it is objectui#8151's own follow-up rather than a card
of its own.
